segments.text: Every unplanned stop costs a factory hours of output. Changing maintenance rules on a real plant floor is expensive and risky. What if you could test thousands of plans before touching a single machine?
Today, plant managers rely on fixed maintenance and dispatch rules. In our simulated plant, the fixed rule delivers only 50.6% of orders on time.
TwinVerdict closes the loop. An open model, Qwen3-8B, proposes policies. A digital twin of the plant scores each one across hundreds of scenarios. The operator gets one clear card, and decides.

On 300 held-out scenarios, on-time orders go from 50.6% to 98.9%. The feedback loop beats a one-shot LLM and the fixed rule. Optuna still scores higher, but needs almost twice the simulations and cannot explain its policy.
Here is the same plant, side by side. Less unplanned downtime, more orders delivered.

The search runs on AMD. Qwen3-8B is served with vLLM on an AMD Instinct MI300X through ROCm, on AMD Developer Cloud. Its large memory keeps the model resident while it answers dozens of requests in parallel.
It is built for plant managers and maintenance engineers. Every number on the card is verified against the simulator before anyone sees it.
And you do not have to take our word for it.
This is the operator card: what to change, why, and the verified impact. Approve or reject.

This is the real recorded run on the MI300X. When the model proposes, the GPU hits 100% at over 500 watts, more than 1,400 tokens per second. Then the simulator takes over. Eight rounds, 37,560 simulations.

Any plant can test its own ideas. Load a policy, simulate, and compare it against the fixed rule in seconds. TwinVerdict. AI proposes, the simulator verifies, the operator decides. Built on AMD. Try it at twinverdict dot focampo dot com.
